Who We Are
Atlan is building the context layer for enterprise AI. Enterprises are pouring money into AI and most of it dies in production because the AI does not understand the business context around the data. That is the problem Atlan solves.

Gartner has named context the defining issue in enterprise AI, and calls context graphs the essential infrastructure for AI agents, naming Atlan one of three vendors already building it. We are also the only vendor named a Leader across all four major Gartner and Forrester evaluations for data catalogs, data governance and metadata management, the foundation the context layer runs on.
Come build the infrastructure that AI runs on.
Atlan is evolving from a world of apps to a world where apps and AI agents work together. The Agent & App Platform team is building the foundational infrastructure that makes this possible.
We’re looking for a Principal Software Engineer to help set the technical direction for the agent registry and gateway platform.
The Team
The Agent & App Platform team builds the foundations that allow Atlan teams, partners, and customers to build, run, distribute, observe, and govern apps and agents reliably at scale.
You’ll work across areas such as:
• 
Agent Registry & Gateways: Systems for registering, discovering, authenticating, governing, and routing agents, tools, and MCP servers.
• 
Agent Platform: Shared capabilities for agent execution, including identity, context, secure execution, sessions, checkpointing, and observability.
• 
App Runtime: Reliable execution infrastructure built on Kubernetes and Temporal.
• 
Distribution & Automation: Packaging, deployment, marketplace experiences, workflows, triggers, templates, and automation capabilities.
What You’ll Do
You’ll own significant technical problems end-to-end and help build the platform primitives powering Atlan’s next generation of apps and agents.
Depending on your strengths and interests, you may:
• 
Design and build platform services for agents, tools, and MCP servers, including registries, gateways, authentication, authorization, routing, policy enforcement, audit logging, and tracing.
• 
Build the primitives that power agent execution and lifecycle — including templates, marketplace experiences, secure sandboxing, tenant-aware context, durable sessions, checkpointing, and observability.
• 
Evolve Atlan’s workflow and runtime infrastructure using Temporal, Kubernetes, and cloud-native technologies, while improving reliability, scalability, performance, and cost.
• 
Design and operate multi-tenant distributed systems for enterprise workloads at significant scale, solving complex problems around isolation, failure recovery, capacity, and noisy neighbours.
• 
Partner with Product and Engineering teams on how apps and agents come together across registration, distribution, and runtime, and contribute to architecture, RFCs, and technical standards.
• 
Mentor engineers and raise the technical bar through strong engineering practices, design reviews, and technical leadership.
What We’re Looking For
• 
14+ years of experience in platform engineering, infrastructure, or backend systems, ideally in a SaaS environment.
• 
Strong experience building platform services, API gateways, service registries, control planes, or similar systems.
• 
Deep expertise in distributed systems and multi-tenant architectures, including event-driven systems, service communication, orchestration, retries, idempotency, and failure recovery.
• 
Strong Kubernetes, containerization, and cloud infrastructure experience across AWS and/or GCP.
• 
Experience designing systems with clear reliability, latency, capacity, and cost requirements, across both 0→1 and mature production environments.
• 
Ability to work autonomously on ambiguous, cross-functional technical problems and communicate complex trade-offs clearly.
It’s a Plus If You Have
• 
Experience with MCP, A2A, agent frameworks, agent runtimes, LLM gateways, or agent observability.
• 
Experience building marketplaces, plugin ecosystems, extension platforms, developer platforms, or workflow/automation systems.
• 
Experience with identity and authorization for non-human actors, secure sandboxing, context propagation, or multi-tenant agent execution.
• 
Experience with Temporal, Terraform, Helm, GitOps, CI/CD, or container registries.
• 
Experience operating enterprise-scale production systems with demanding SLOs, observability, distributed tracing, or cost attribution.
How We Work
We’re building an AI-native engineering organization and use AI-assisted development tools such as Claude and Cursor as part of our everyday workflow.
You’ll thrive here if you take strong ownership, enjoy ambiguous technical problems, communicate clearly, learn quickly, and care about building reusable primitives, reliable systems, and great developer experiences.
The Technology
Go · Python · AWS · GCP · Kubernetes · Karpenter · Temporal · MCP · Terraform · Helm · Prometheus · Grafana · GitOps
You don’t need experience with every technology listed above. We care more about strong engineering fundamentals, distributed-systems expertise, and the ability to learn quickly.

Why Atlan?
Joining Atlan means being part of a global movement to help data teams do their life’s best work. Here’s what you can expect:
• 
Competitive Compensation: We benchmark at the top of the market and keep compensation simple: strong base salary, performance‑based variable pay, and impact‑driven equity (for most roles), so your total rewards grow in step with the value you create over time.
• 
AI Native Culture: Atlan is where AI-native builders come to build the systems the future of work will run on. AI isn’t an add-on, it’s woven into how we build, think, and work every day, empowering every Atlanian to move faster and create a bigger impact.
• 
Health & Wellness: From Day‑1 health, dental, vision, and mental health to flexible health stipends, we design benefits offerings that lead in each country we're in.
• 
Flexible Time Off & Leave Policies: We trust you to own your energy: flexible time off and modern leave so you can unplug properly, support yourself and your loved ones, and come back ready to drive an impact.
• 
Accelerated Growth & Learning: Develop at an uncommon velocity through cutting-edge tech, complex implementations, and an experienced team that values mastery.
• 
Global, Remote-First, High-Trust: Work from anywhere with a diverse team across 15+ countries, in a trust-first, async environment that gives you true flexibility and ownership over how you work.

More About Us
Atlan is building the shared context layer that enterprises need so AI can operate on trusted, governed context. The conversation has moved from data leaders asking: “Can we trust the data in our stack?” to businesses asking: “Can we trust AI inside the business?”
We are the missing infrastructure for businesses becoming AI-forward - the connective tissue between their data stack, operational systems, and AI agents.

To learn more, visit www.atlan.com and follow us on LinkedIn.

Equal Opportunity Employer
Atlan is committed to building an inclusive, diverse, and authentic workplace. We do not discriminate based on race, color, religion, national origin, age, disability, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, marital status, military or veteran status, or any other legally protected characteristic.

Mission
Neko is redefining what prevention means, from treating illness when it arrives, to sustaining health before it's ever at risk. Our mission: make data-driven, preventative care accessible to more people, before symptoms appear. 

In a single, non-invasive visit under an hour, proprietary technology and direct clinical care combine to deliver personalised, actionable insights. It's a team that thinks in 10x, not 10%. Every role here plays a part in building a world where prevention is the norm, and where your work genuinely helps people live longer, healthier lives.

Role Purpose
The Practice Manager owns practice management for Neko Health's United States professional corporation. The role covers four areas: provider credentialing, SOP organization and maintenance, onboarding operationalization, and compliance assurance. Neko runs a tech-enabled clinical model, and this role is expected to run all four through systems and automation rather than manual tracking.
Credentialing: the role holds the credential file for every provider practicing under the PC: license, certification, permitted scope by state, malpractice coverage details and every other expirable, verified at source and kept current so that no provider ever sees a member on a lapsed credential. While Neko does not credential with payers today - this role runs the credentialing gate that clears a provider to practice and removes that clearance when a credential lapses. It supplies provider credentialing data into the clinic compliance systems and works to the credentialing standard and clear-to-practice definition set by the Head of Compliance.
SOPs: the role owns the SOP library for US practice operations. The role keeps every SOP current, versioned, and easy to find, and retires SOPs that no longer apply.
Onboarding: the role turns each new provider's onboarding plan into a working, tracked sequence: credentialing, system access, training, and clearance to start, in the right order and against a clear timeline.
Compliance: the role checks that US practice operations meet the standards set by the Head of Compliance, and reports gaps as they surface.
Systems and automation: the role chooses, configures and owns the tooling that carries all of the above — one source of truth for provider data, automated expiry alerts, and workflows that hand off cleanly between Talent Acquisition, the People Team, IT and clinical operations. Status should be visible from the system rather than assembled by hand.
As Neko opens further states, credentialing volume and complexity grow faster than headcount, and practice operations grow with them. This role exists to make provider readiness, SOP currency, onboarding execution, and compliance standing a managed process with evidence behind it, built on tooling that scales faster than headcount, rather than a scramble before each launch.
What You'll Deliver in the First 6–12 Months
• 
A current, auditable register of every clinician's license, credential, and permitted scope by state, held in a single system of record with automated expiry tracking and a named process for renewal before lapse.
• 
A complete credential file per provider practicing under the PC, with primary source verification evidence attached and dated.
• 
A written credentialing procedure covering intake, verification, the clear-to-practice decision, re-verification cycle, and removal of clearance.
• 
The credentialing gate built into the clinician onboarding sequence, so a start date cannot be confirmed without verified credentials.
• 
A current SOP library for US practice operations: indexed, version-controlled, and reviewed on a set cycle.
• 
An onboarding operations sequence that turns each new provider's plan into a tracked timeline from offer to start, with the credentialing gate built in.
• 
Practice operations running in-system rather than on spreadsheets: onboarding, SOP review cycles and compliance checks tracked in Neko's tooling, with the remaining manual steps documented and a plan to remove them.
• 
A compliance status report showing where US practice operations meet the Head of Compliance's standards, and where they do not, generated from the system rather than compiled by hand.
Key Responsibilities
Provider credentialing and primary source verification
• 
Run credentialing intake for every new provider joining the PC: application, document collection, and verification at source rather than from candidate-supplied copies.
• 
Verify state medical/nursing licenses, board certification, education and training, work history, and DEA registration where the provider's scope requires it.
• 
Operate the clear-to-practice gate: no provider is released to see members until the credential file is complete and verified.
• 
Maintain the permitted scope by state for each provider and flag to the Head of Compliance any request to practice outside it.
Expirables, re-verification and removal
• 
Own the expirables calendar for licenses, certifications, DEA registrations, malpractice coverage and any other time-limited credential, driven by automated alerts rather than manual review.
• 
Chase renewals ahead of expiry against defined lead times and escalate when a renewal is at risk.
• 
Remove clearance to practice immediately when a credential lapses and notify the clinical rota owner and the Head of Compliance the same day.
• 
Run the re-verification cycle so credential files do not silently age.
Systems, tooling and automation
• 
Select, implement and administer the tooling that runs practice operations: credentialing records, expiry tracking, onboarding workflow and SOP version control.
• 
Replace manual tracking with automated alerts, scheduled reporting and system-driven handoffs, and keep a running list of the steps still done by hand.
• 
Define the data structure behind credentialing and onboarding so status can be reported out of the system rather than reconstructed.
• 
Work with IT and, where relevant, product and engineering to integrate practice operations data with adjacent systems instead of maintaining parallel spreadsheets.
SOP organization and maintenance
• 
Own the SOP library for US practice operations: create, index, and version every procedure.
• 
Review each SOP on a set cycle and update it when a process changes.
• 
Retire SOPs that no longer apply, and flag processes that run without one.
• 
Keep SOPs easy to find and use for the staff who rely on them day to day.
Onboarding operationalization
• 
Turn each new provider's onboarding plan into a tracked sequence: credentialing, system access, training, and clearance to start.
• 
Own the onboarding timeline from offer to start date, and flag delays before they hit the start date.
• 
Coordinate with Talent Acquisition, the People Team, and clinical operations to keep the sequence moving.
• 
Improve the onboarding sequence as volume grows, including automation of tracking and reminders.
Compliance assurance
• 
Confirm that US practice operations meet the standards set by the Head of Compliance.
• 
Run periodic checks against those standards, and report gaps as they surface.
• 
Support audits of practice operations with evidence drawn from SOPs, onboarding records, and the credentialing file.
• 
Escalate compliance gaps that need action beyond this role.
Credentialing process, data and reporting
• 
Keep the credentialing record system accurate and audit-ready, so a credential file can be produced on request without reconstruction.
• 
Report credentialing status, upcoming expiries and blocked providers into the Medical Quality reporting cycle, on a set cadence and drawn from the system of record.
• 
Improve the credentialing process as volume grows, including automation of tracking and reminders.
• 
Prepare the function for payer credentialing and provider enrollment should Neko US move to billing insurance.
